title: Illustration / Characters / Noses
slide_intent: Construct and color a nose as part of the face so it adds definition without becoming a distracting feature.
strategic_value: Simple forms with controlled color relationships can help Duolingo preserve legible faces across its varied cast.
demonstration: Three approved face examples appear above two rejected nose-color examples in crossed frames; the right column describes form, size and profile color.
practical_value: Use 1–2 rounded rectangles, choose size for the character and evaluate darkness together with saturation.

content_islands.name: Nose-color comparisons
content_islands.spec: Place three faces with different skin and nose colors across the top left; put two rejected color treatments below inside red crossed frames.

content_islands.name: Construction and color guidance
content_islands.spec: Place the Noses heading and paragraph at right, including the profile-view skin-color condition.

reference_purposes.Application: The face specimens compare nose treatments across different skin colors.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source specifies 1–2 rounded rectangles, leaves size to the character, ties saturation to darkness qualitatively and makes the nose match the base skin tone in profile.

ingredient.name: Simple nose construction
ingredient.role: Define the face without introducing an unrelated visual accent.
ingredient.application: Build the nose from 1–2 rounded rectangles; choose size for the character, balance saturation with darkness, and match base skin tone in profile.
ingredient.scope: Historical official Duolingo illustration guidance from the 2024–2025 archived snapshot. The saturation-versus-darkness instruction is qualitative; the source gives no numeric color ratio.
